entries.title: What to know about diarrhea-causing cyclosporiasis in Illinois
entries.summary: <p>Illinois has confirmed 309 cases of the diarrhea-causing illness cyclosporiasis, the state’s public health department confirmed Friday.</p><p>Cyclosporiasis is not considered deadly and is more of an inconvenience that in rare cases could have complications, said Dr. Emily Landon, an infectious diseases specialist at University of Chicago Medicine. In Illinois, 24 people have been hospitalized, according to the Illinois Department of Public Health. Most of the people in Illinois who have contracted the illness had traveled recently — 125 people internationally and 152<b> </b>domestically. It’s unclear if the other 32 traveled.</p><p>Higher numbers of cyclosporiasis are typically reported in the summer, but this year has seen an especially high number, health officials said.</p><p>The increase in Illinois is part of a larger number of cases in most states. Across 34 states, 1,645 cases have been reported, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.</p><p>Here's what you need to know about cyclosporiasis in Illinois.</p><h3><b>What is cyclosporiasis?</b></h3><p>Pronounced sigh-klo-spore-EYE-uh-sis, cyclosporiasis is an intestinal illness caused by the microscopic parasite cyclospora. Infection often comes after eating fresh fruits and vegetables and can lead to watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, gas and nausea.</p><p>The heat-loving parasite infects the bowels and spreads through feces. In the past, people have been infected by consuming fruits or vegetables that were exposed to feces-contaminated irrigation water. </p><h3><b>What is causing cyclosporiasis in Illinois?</b></h3><p>No definitive source has been identified for the Illinois cases, but Taylor Fresh Foods, a California-based farm and food company, voluntarily recalled iceberg salad and shredded lettuce products distributed in 27 states, including Illinois. In other states, Marketside-brand iceberg products sold at select Walmart stores were also recalled. </p><p>The FDA on Sunday said that initial testing for cyclospora in a sample of lettuce from Taylor Farms was a false positive. The products in question from Taylor Farms were grown in the Mexican state of Guanajuato.</p><p>The voluntary recall comes days after the <a class="Link" href="https://www.cdc.gov/cyclosporiasis/outbreaks/07-26/index.html" target="_blank" >CDC</a> identified shredded lettuce served at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky, Ohio and West Virginia as a source of widespread outbreaks in those states. In a statement, Taco Bell announced it was removing the affected lettuce from its supply chain across the country and planned to replace it in select states. Taylor Farms supplied lettuce to Taco Bell, The New York Times reported.</p><p>Past outbreaks have been linked to imported fresh produce, like bagged salad kits and berries, according to IDPH. Cyclosporiasis is not transmitted from person to person, Landon said. Even if a person becomes sick, people don’t usually contaminate objects in their house enough to spread it to someone else.</p><h3><b>How long does it take to recover?</b></h3><p>People should talk to their doctor about getting tested if they have symptoms, so health officials can continue to track the outbreak, said Gwen Biggerstaff, the CDC’s deputy director of foodborne, waterborne and environmental diseases.</p><p>Most people who contract the illness recover in one to two weeks, according to the CDC. Many can recover with rest and plenty of fluids, but some may need antibiotics.</p><p>People can experience bloating, gas and dehydration but rarely have more complications.</p><p>“The problem with this disease is it can be kind of persistent,” Landon said. “And you can feel pretty sick, and then you can be starting to get better, and then the diarrhea can come back again.” </p><h3><b>Should I stop eating fresh fruits and vegetables? </b></h3><p>If a person is immunocompromised or has an underlying medical condition, they should take more precautions, Landon said. That’s especially true, for example, for those undergoing surgery soon or cancer treatments.</p><p>Everyone can follow typical food safety guidelines like washing hands and thoroughly washing and scrubbing fresh produce. Illinois health officials also suggest:</p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0;padding-inline-start:48px;" id="rte-b5494250-808c-11f1-a776-3b92d1e3bbf6"><li>Incorporating more fruits and vegetables with peels or outer layers</li><li>Eating canned fruits and vegetables</li><li>Keeping produce separate from raw meat and seafood</li><li>Refrigerating cut, peeled, or cooked fruits and vegetables within two hours</li><li>Refrigerating perishable produce.</li><li>Cooking vegetables to at least 158 degrees Fahrenheit </li></ul><h3><b>Is it safer to buy produce from my local Illinois farmers market? </b></h3><p>Fruits and vegetables coming from a smaller, local producer are likely to have less of a risk for contamination than food from massive manufacturers, Landon said. That’s especially true if an outbreak is centered on a certain product, but officials this time around don’t know if that’s the case.</p><p>So you shouldn’t assume there’s zero risk in buying from a local vendor because any farm can become contaminated, especially because of the current weather, Landon said.</p><p>Vendors at Chicago farmers markets haven’t seen a decline in sales so far, but they have gotten more questions from customers.</p><p>“We are quite confident that it is not coming from our farm or any of the other local family farms around us,” said Christina Gelder of Ellis Family Farms. She added that they are in close contact with Michigan State University to track research related to the cyclosporiasis outbreak.</p><p>Chelsa Moore shopped for produce at the Pullman Farmers Market after going down a “rabbit hole” searching for best practices to avoid getting sick. She’s avoiding prepackaged food and triple rinsing produce at home.</p><p>“I’m kind of leaning toward the side of just like not buying anything from the big stores and going to the local farmers market,” she said. “And then even doing even more with prepping and cleaning.” </p><h3><b>How is Illinois tracking the cases?</b></h3><p>The Illinois Department of Public Health is working with local health officials to collect data on the cases. They are also working with the CDC to investigate a potential source of the illness.</p><p>The Chicago Department of Public Health as of Friday had not identified the source of local cases. One individual had eaten at Taco Bell but had also traveled to one of the states that is part of the larger outbreak. The department is seeing an increase in cases among Latinos who had not recently traveled internationally.</p><p>The number of cases locally and across the country could be higher, Landon said. That’s because testing for cyclosporiasis is expensive, and some insurance may not cover it. But as cases of cyclosporiasis are more in the news, doctors will likely start testing more patients or prescribe antibiotics to treat it if someone has symptoms.</p><p>If a person is confirmed to have cyclosporiasis, Landon said it’s important to cooperate with the local health department to detail everything they ate so officials can pinpoint the outbreak source.</p><h3><b>Are federal cuts affecting the outbreak? </b></h3><p>Last summer, the federal government scaled back a program known as the Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network that monitored foodborne illnesses, <a class="Link" href="https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/cdc-quietly-scaled-back-surveillance-program-foodborne-illnesses-rcna227089?link_source=ta_bluesky_link&taid=68add0b9b2316600014ce6de&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_medium=social&utm_source=bluesky" target="_blank" ><u>NBC News previously reported</u></a>. As part of the changes, reporting for cyclospora parasites became optional in 2025, according to the program’s website. The government had previously collected that data since 1997.</p><p>The scaled-back federal program worked with the FDA to proactively test certain foods to check if recalls were necessary, Landon said.</p><p>It’s hard to assess how much changes on the federal level are playing a role in the current outbreaks, Landon said. But it’s something health officials across the country should consider.</p><p>“It’s a combination of the nature of the illness, the fact that it’s happening at a time when there’s other sporadic cases, and then the lack of infrastructure and resources available for testing does matter,” Landon said, summing up the factors driving the outbreak. <br></p>

entries.title: Lionel Messi says 'pain is huge' after World Cup loss to Spain
entries.summary: <p>Lionel Messi said "the pain is huge" after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain, but the legendary figure added he will cherish good memories from the competition.</p><p>Spain defeated Messi’s Argentina team 1-0 in extra time on Sunday, July 19, at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.</p><p>It was the third World Cup final for Messi, who has now lost two (2014 and 2026) and won one (2022) in his illustrious career.</p><p>Messi was in tears after the final whistle. At 39, he has likely played his final World Cup game.</p><p>The Inter Miami forward didn't speak to the press following the final, but he released a message on Instagram Monday.</p><p>"The pain is huge, and this wound will take time to heal," Messi wrote on social media. "But I also hold onto all the good things. … The matches we turned around by giving it our all — moments that will remain in our memories forever — and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group's hard work and effort, brought us back among the world's elite once again.</p><p>"It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals.</p><p>"Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.</p><p>"I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship."</p><div entries.title: En audiencia, la Policía de Chicago dice que ha implementado la orden del alcalde para investigar a ICE
entries.summary: <p>Funcionarios de la Ciudad de Chicago fueron convocados a una tensa audiencia del comité del Concejo Municipal el viernes para brindar respuestas sobre la implementación tardía de la orden del alcalde Brandon Johnson que instruye al Departamento de Policía de Chicago (CPD) a investigar posibles delitos cometidos por agentes federales de inmigración.</p><p>Los miembros del Comité de Derechos de Inmigrantes y Refugiados pasaron aproximadamente dos horas interrogando a los asistentes del alcalde y a los líderes policiales sobre la orden ejecutiva de Johnson, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/07/15/orden-alcalde-chicago-contra-agentes-enfrenta-fuerte-escrutinio-concejales" target="_blank" >“ICE on Notice” (“ICE sobre aviso”)</a>, para saber qué ha logrado el decreto y qué pasos adicionales son necesarios para hacerla cumplir.</p><p>Los funcionarios de la policía dijeron que el departamento había concluido los procedimientos internos para implementar la orden, casi cinco meses después del <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/02/02/alcalde-de-chicago-ordena-al-departamento-de-policia-investigar-a-los-agentes-federales-de-inmigracion" target="_blank" >plazo de 30 días</a> establecido por el alcalde. Sin embargo, no quisieron explicar por qué tomó tanto tiempo.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-780000" name="module-780000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>“Valoramos a CPD y queremos creer que los oficiales están aquí para preservar y proteger nuestras comunidades. Pero ya es hora de que haya responsabilidad ante el público”, dijo el concejal Andre Vasquez (40.°), presidente del comité.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" target="_blank" >Operativo Midway Blitz</a>, la campaña de deportación agresiva de la administración de Trump el otoño pasado.</p><p>Pero el llamado hizo poco para calmar las frustraciones de los concejales y de los miembros de la comunidad.</p><p>Los miembros del comité llegaron preparados con una lista de preguntas: ¿Cómo hará cumplir el departamento de policía las nuevas políticas? ¿Ha sido notificado todo el departamento de los cambios? ¿Y quién puede presentar un reporte de policía si alguien es detenido por un agente federal?.</p><p>Los funcionarios de la policía dijeron que el departamento carecía de un sistema para rastrear las quejas contra agentes federales. Eso significa que tuvieron que establecer nuevos protocolos para investigar esas quejas, recolectar evidencia e identificar a los agentes federales involucrados.</p><p>Se les ha indicado a los oficiales que obtengan declaraciones de testigos y presenten informes, pero el departamento no abrirá casos criminales a menos que una víctima o un familiar de la víctima se presente.</p><p>“Debemos trabajar de acuerdo con los deseos de la víctima y con lo que esta quiere que hagamos, ya sea continuar con el informe de caso realizado o no”, dijo Patrick Kinney, comandante de la Oficina de Detectives.</p><p>Si una víctima no puede presentar un informe, un familiar puede hacerlo en su lugar, dijeron los funcionarios. Eso incluye casos en los que alguien es detenido por agentes federales y los miembros de su familia no pueden localizarlo. La policía puede iniciar una investigación sobre la conducta del agente y las circunstancias que rodean la detención.</p><p>En el comunicado de prensa del viernes, la oficina de Johnson indicó que el departamento de policía está revisando un informe emitido en abril por la <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/05/04/comision-que-investiga-el-operativo-midway-blitz-sienta-las-bases-para-una-verdadera-rendicion-de-cuentas" target="_blank" >Comisión de Responsabilidad de Illinois</a>, convocada por el gobernador JB Pritzker para investigar abusos cometidos por agentes del Operativo Midway Blitz. Se instó a las personas nombradas en el informe —y a otros que “fueron testigos o experimentaron conductas ilegales”— a ponerse en contacto con el departamento de policía.</p><p>Durante la ofensiva de cumplimiento del año pasado, residentes de la ciudad —e incluso policías— fueron <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2025/11/13/tear-gas-federal-agents-immigration-enforcement-chicago-police-department-dan-oconnor" target="_blank" >expuestos a gases lacrimógenos</a>. Los agentes federales <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2025/11/14/ice-bovino-border-patrol-homeland-security-chicago-police-department" target="_blank" >provocaron accidentes de tráfico</a> mientras realizaban arrestos. Una <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/02/04/marimar-martinez-baleada-por-agentes-de-migracion-se-pronuncia-contra-asesinatos" target="_blank" >mujer fue baleada cinco veces</a> en el lado suroeste de la ciudad y un padre inmigrante murió <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2025/11/18/silverio-villegas-gonzalez-asesinado-por-agente-de-ice-en-area-de-chicago-tenia-cocaina-en-el-sistema-autopsia" target="_blank" >tras ser herido de </figure> </div> </div><p>Los funcionarios de la policía dijeron que están buscando testigos y pruebas. Indicaron que utilizarán imágenes de las cámaras de la policía y de los lectores de placas para investigar los informes de delitos.</p><p>Y mientras afirmaron que cierta información podría ser divulgada públicamente, la evidencia y otros materiales de investigación seguirán siendo confidenciales para preservar la integridad de cualquier posible enjuiciamiento penal.</p><p>“Nuestra mayor preocupación es asegurarnos de que cualquier evidencia que se nos presente pueda presentarse en la corte”, dijo Kinney. “La cadena de custodia es extremadamente importante para nosotros”.</p><p>La audiencia se llevó a cabo en medio de lo que los defensores locales han descrito como <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/07/16/defensores-de-inmigrantes-en-chicago-exigen-abolir-ice-tras-tiroteos-mortales-en-houston-y-maine" target="_blank" >un aumento en la aplicación de la ley de inmigración</a> y tras dos tiroteos fatales que involucraron a agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) en Texas y Maine.</p><p>Ningún agente de inmigración ha sido acusado de cometer delitos en el ejercicio de sus funciones en el Condado de Cook, a pesar de los fuertes llamados a la rendición de cuentas. La fiscal del estado del Condado de Cook, Eileen O’Neill Burke, ha sostenido que le corresponde a la policía investigar y remitir los casos a su oficina para su acusación.</p><p>Esa postura fue respaldada por la jueza del circuito del Condado de Cook, Erica Reddick, quien rechazó una solicitud para <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/05/26/jueza-del-condado-de-cook-rechaza-nombrar-fiscal-especial-para-investigar-agentes-de-operativo-midway-blitz" target="_blank" >designar a un fiscal especial</a> para investigar delitos alegados por agentes federales de inmigración.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: The World Cup is over, but soccer goes on. Here's where to get your next fix
entries.summary: <p>After 39 days and 104 matches, the World Cup has come to an end.</p><p>No more videos of Scottish fans putting traffic cones on statues and taking over baseball stadiums. No more clips of fans in tears of joy over what they just witnessed. No more screaming "Country Roads" or Viking rows.</p><p>If you're a new fan of soccer, you might be thinking, "Now what?"</p><p>Well, for one thing, big summer tournaments aren't too far away — the Women's World Cup in Brazil starts in June 2027, while the United Kingdom will host the men's Euros in 2028.</p><p>But soccer never actually takes much of a break (as the exhausted players can attest).</p><p>In just a few weeks, some of the game's biggest stars will be back with their clubs, getting ready for new seasons in England's Premier League, Spain's La Liga and Germany's Bundesliga, to name a few. And then, of course, there's the Champions League, where Europe's best sides face each other.</p><p>Here's a guide to some of the biggest leagues in the world — and how you can follow them — to help solve even the most acute cases of World Cup withdrawal.</p><h3>Premier League</h3><h3></h3><p>The richest league in the world features heavyweights like Arsenal and Manchester City, as well as plucky — and increasingly competitive — underdogs like Bournemouth and Brighton & Hove Albion.</p><p>Supporters create an incredible atmosphere with creative — and frequently expletive-filled — chants aimed at the opposition. And with so many personalities, both among the players and the highly stressed coaches, each 38-match season invariably turns into a soap opera.</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>• Erling Haaland, Manchester City: The Norwegian striker's goofy personality took social media by storm this summer, but he's even more famous for scoring 112 Premier League goals in just four seasons for Man City.</p><p>• Enzo Fernández, Chelsea: Chelsea's social media team got in hot water after they celebrated the midfielder's stunning goal in Argentina's semifinal win last week. Fernández's strike, after all, had helped eliminate England.</p><p>• Bukayo Saka, Arsenal: Nicknamed "Starboy," the English midfielder dazzles on the right for Arsenal, which just won its first league title in 22 years.</p><p>• Tyler Adams, Bournemouth: The hard-tackling American has been a fixture in Bournemouth's midfield since 2023.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b></p><p>Matches are mostly held on Saturdays and Sundays, though weekday matches aren't uncommon. But be prepared to get up early, especially if you live on the West Coast. Many matches take place at 9 a.m. Chicago time, and there is usually an early-riser at 6:30 a.m., with a marquee match at 11:30 a.m. Many of the biggest games are shown on NBC, while others are shown on USA Network or Peacock. Get used to checking online listings to decipher it all.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> Aug. 21.-May 30.</p><h3>La Liga</h3><h3></h3><p>It's a league long dominated by Real Madrid and Barcelona. The two titans have won 11 of the past 12 league titles and, twice a year, they square off in El Clásico, one of the world's fiercest rivalry matches. Beyond that, the league is a showcase for creative, attacking talent.</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>• Jude Bellingham, Real Madrid: England's 23-year-old midfielder scored seven goals in the He's not too shabby at Real Madrid either, scoring 25 goals in La Liga last season.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b></p><p>Matches typically start a few hours later than Premier League ones, making it more accessible to U.S. fans who aren't morning people. Every match is available on the ESPN+ app, with some of the bigger matchups also available on either ABC, ESPN or ESPN2.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> Aug. 15.-May 30</p><h3>Bundesliga</h3><h3></h3><p>With relentless singing from the fans in the crowd and relentless attacking from the players on the field, the Bundesliga makes for great TV. Borussia Dortmund's famed "Yellow Wall" of fans is especially intimidating. Just don't be surprised when Bayern Munich wins the title yet again.</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>• Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: England's captain has dominated the Bundesliga ever since joining Germany's most decorated club in 2023.</p><p>• Michael Olise, Bayern Munich: The winger produced some of the most exciting performances in the World Cup as part of France's devastating attack.</p><p>• Yan Diomandé, RB Leipzig: The 19-year-old had a fantastic World Cup for the Ivory Coast and has caught the eye of various Premier League giants. Leipzig insists he is not for sale.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b></p><p>The Bundesliga just signed an English-language deal with USA Network and Fandango. You're forgiven for not knowing that Fandango, a company famous for selling movie tickets, is getting into sports broadcasting.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> Aug. 28.-May 22</p><h3>Champions League</h3><p>Each year, the top clubs in each European league qualify for the Champions League. The opening phase involves 36 clubs playing eight games apiece. From there, the field is whittled down through knockout rounds before ending with a final in a major European city. The next one will be in Madrid.</p><p>If you are looking for soccer of the highest technical quality, the Champions League is your answer. Unlike the World Cup, where teams have limited time together before the tournament, Champions League clubs are finely tuned squads that practice together nearly year-round. For many fans, winning a Champions League trophy is an even bigger prize than a league title.</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p> Pretty much all the European-based heavyweights will be there. Well, not Chelsea: They finished 10th in the Premier League last season, far too low to qualify.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b></p><p>This is when work can get in the way, since most matches occur on Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons if you're on the East Coast. Every match is available to stream on Paramount+, with marquee ones also broadcast on CBS, including the final — which often commands a larger global audience than the Super Bowl.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> The league phase kicks off Sept. 8., with the final on June 5, 2027.</p><h3>MLS</h3><p>Unlike the major European leagues, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fire" >MLS is well underway,</a> despite a hiatus during the World Cup. So if you're looking for a soccer fix, you only have to wait until Wednesday night, when you can take your pick between 15 different matches, including the Fire at Inter Miami at 6:30 p.m.</p><p>The quality on the field might not be as strong as elite European competition, but the league has gotten steadily better over the past two decades, with clubs largely prioritizing exciting young talents over aging stars (though some teams still go down that route, too, for better or worse).</p><p>The action is also quite unpredictable: Thanks in part to strict spending limits, dynasties are rare — no team has won the title two years in a row since 2012 — giving fans of each team hope at the start of the season.</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>• Lionel Messi, Inter Miami: Some thought that joining MLS in 2023 would cause the Argentine legend to lose his edge as he approaches 40. Those doubters were wrong.</p><p>• Son Heung-min, LAFC: South Korea's biggest star had a disappointing World Cup, and he recently scored his first MLS goal of the season. But fans still pack downtown Los Angeles to see the beloved 34-year-old striker.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/IkR7BiDXfRI?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Son Heung-Min Scores His First Goal of the Season!"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>• Matt Freese, NYCFC: The U.S. goalkeeper has impressed for NYCFC, though it might take awhile for U.S. fans to look past his blunder against Belgium.</p><p>• Robert Lewandowski, Fire: The Polish star last played for Barcelona before signing with the Fire this summer. His MLS debut was delayed when smoke from Canadian wildfires force the Fire to postpone a July 16 match against Vancouver.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b> </p><p>The vast majority of the matches are on weekend nights. All of them are available on Apple TV, with some also shown on Fox Sports 1.</p><p><b>2026 SEASON DATES:</b> The regular season began Feb. 21 and will run through Nov. 7, with playoffs to follow.</p><h3>Liga MX</h3><p>You thought the Premier League was the most-watched league in the U.S.? Think again: That honor actually goes to the Mexican league, which sees huge Hispanic audiences tune in for their favorite clubs, including rivals Club América and Chivas de Guadalajara. Not only are the rivalries intense, but there are also two winners each year, thanks to a split-season format that crowns one champion in the fall (Apertura) and another in the spring (Clausura).</p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>• Gilberto Mora, Club Tijuana: Mexico fans fell in love with the 17-year-old attacking midfielder during El Tri's run to the round of 16.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b> </p><p>Some matches are available in English via the CBS Sports Network or Fox Sports. But most of the viewership comes for the Spanish-language broadcasters, including Univision and Telemundo.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> The regular Apertura campaign began July 16, and will conclude in December. The Clausura campaign will take place in early 2027.</p><p></p><h3><b>NWSL </b></h3><p>This is the place to be if you’re looking to get revved up for next year’s Women’s World Cup. The Chicago Stars' next match is at 7 p.m. Friday against the Orlando Pride on Victory+. </p><p><b>WHO PLAYS THERE</b></p><p>Mallory Swanson, Stars: The 2019 Women's World Cup and 2024 Olympic champion returned to the Stars earlier this season. </p><p>Trinity Rodman, Washington Spirit: Rodman is part of the "Triple Espresso" (along with Swanson and Sophia Wilson) that led the United States to a gold medal at the 2024 Olympics in Paris.</p><p><b>HOW TO WATCH</b></p><p>Matches are available on a variety of outlets, including ESPN, CBS, CBSSN, Paramount+, Prime Video, Ion, Disney+, NWSL+ and Victory+.</p><p><b>2026-2027 SEASON DATES:</b> The season started March 13 and concluded with the championship match on Nov. 1.</p>

entries.title: Lo que debes saber sobre la ciclosporiasis, que está causando diarrea a los habitantes de  Illinois
entries.summary: <p>En Illinois se han confirmado 309 casos de la enfermedad diarreica causada por la ciclosporiasis, confirmó el Departamento de Salud Pública del estado el viernes.</p><p>La ciclosporiasis no se considera mortal; es más una molestia que en raras ocasiones podría tener complicaciones, explicó la Dra. Emily Landon, especialista en enfermedades infecciosas de la Universidad de Medicina de Chicago.</p><p>En Illinois, 24 personas han sido hospitalizadas, según el Departamento de Salud Pública de Illinois (IDPH). La mayoría de las personas en Illinois que han contraído la enfermedad viajaron recientemente: 125 personas a nivel internacional y 152 a nivel nacional. No está claro si las otras 32 personas viajaron.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-4f0000" name="module-4f0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Normalmente se reportan más casos de ciclosporiasis en el verano, pero este año se ha observado un número especialmente alto, dijeron las autoridades sanitarias.</p><p>El aumento en Illinois forma parte de un número más amplio de casos en la mayoría de los estados. En 34 estados, se han reportado 1,645 casos, según los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC).</p><p>Esto es lo que necesitas saber sobre la ciclosporiasis en Illinois.</p><h3>¿Qué es la ciclosporiasis?</h3><p>La ciclosporiasis es una enfermedad intestinal causada por el parásito microscópico Cyclospora cayetanensis. La infección a menudo ocurre tras consumir frutas y verduras frescas y puede provocar diarrea acuosa, calambres estomacales, gas y náuseas.</p><p>El parásito, que ama el calor, infecta los intestinos y se propaga a través de las heces. En el pasado, las personas se han infectado al consumir frutas o verduras expuestas a agua de riego contaminada con heces.</p><h3>¿Qué está causando la ciclosporiasis en Illinois?</h3><p>No se ha identificado una fuente definitiva del brote actual en Illinois, pero los brotes anteriores han estado relacionados con productos frescos importados, como ensaladas preparadas y frutos rojos, según el departamento de salud del estado.</p><p>La ciclosporiasis no se transmite de persona a persona, dijo Landon. Incluso si una persona se enferma, generalmente no contamina objetos en su casa lo suficiente como para contagiar a otra persona.</p><h3>¿Cuánto tiempo toma recuperarse?</h3><p>Las personas deben hablar con su médico sobre hacerse pruebas si presentan síntomas, para que las autoridades de salud puedan continuar rastreando el brote, dijo Gwen Biggerstaff, subdirectora de enfermedades transmitidas por alimentos, agua y medio ambiente de los CDC.</p><p>La mayoría de las personas que contraen la enfermedad se recuperan en una o dos semanas, según los CDC. Muchas pueden recuperarse con descanso y mucha hidratación, pero algunas pueden necesitar antibióticos.</p><p>Las personas pueden experimentar hinchazón, gas y deshidratación, pero rara vez presentan complicaciones adicionales.</p><p>“El problema con esta enfermedad es que puede ser un poco persistente”, señaló Landon. “Y puedes sentirte bastante enfermo, y luego puedes empezar a sentirte mejor, y después la diarrea puede regresar nuevamente”.</p><h3>¿Debo dejar de comer frutas y verduras frescas?</h3><p>Si una persona está inmunocomprometida o tiene una condición médica subyacente, debe tomar más precauciones, dijo Landon. Eso es especialmente cierto, por ejemplo, para aquellos que van a someterse a una cirugía pronto o a tratamientos contra el cáncer.</p><p>Todos pueden seguir pautas típicas de seguridad alimentaria, como lavarse las manos y lavar y fregar bien las frutas y verduras frescas. Las autoridades de salud de Illinois también sugieren:</p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-bead1ea0-8476-11f1-b7a6-dd58942b55c0"><li>Incorporar más frutas y verduras con cáscaras o capas exteriores</li><li>Consumir frutas y verduras enlatadas</li><li>Mantener las frutas y verduras separadas de la carne y los mariscos crudos</li><li>Refrigerar las frutas y verduras cortadas, peladas o cocidas dentro de dos horas</li><li>Refrigerar productos perecederos</li><li>Cocinar las verduras a por lo menos 158 grados Fahrenheit</li></ul><h3>¿<b>Es más seguro comprar productos en mi mercado local de Illinois? </b></h3><p>Las frutas y verduras provenientes de un productor local más pequeño tienen menos riesgo de contaminación que los alimentos de grandes fabricantes, dijo Landon. Eso es especialmente cierto si un brote se centra en un producto específico, pero las autoridades no saben si ese es el caso esta vez.</p><p>Por lo tanto, no debes asumir que no hay riesgo al comprar a un vendedor local, porque cualquier granja puede contaminarse, especialmente debido al clima actual, destacó Landon.</p><p>Los vendedores de los mercados locales de Chicago no han observado una disminución de las ventas hasta ahora, pero han recibido más preguntas de los clientes.</p><p>“Estamos bastante seguros de que no proviene de nuestra granja ni de ninguna de las otras granjas familiares locales a nuestro alrededor”, dijo Christina Gelder de Ellis Family Farms. Agregó que están en contacto cercano con la Universidad Estatal de Michigan para rastrear la investigación relacionada con el brote de ciclosporiasis.</p><p>Chelsa Moore compró productos en el Pullman Farmers Market tras buscarinformación sobre las mejores prácticas para prevenir enfermedades. Está evitando alimentos preenvasados y enjuagando los productos en casa tres veces.</p><p>“Estoy un poco inclinada a no comprar nada en las tiendas grandes e ir al mercado local”, dijo. “Y luego, incluso hacer más en cuanto a la preparación y la limpieza”.</p><h3>¿<b>Cómo está Illinois rastreando los casos? </b></h3><p>El Departamento de Salud Pública de Illinois está trabajando con funcionarios de salud locales para recopilar datos sobre los casos. También están colaborando con los CDC para investigar una posible fuente de la enfermedad.</p><p>Los <a class="Link" href="https://www.cdc.gov/cyclosporiasis/outbreaks/07-26/index.html" target="_blank" >CDC</a> han identificado la lechuga rallada servida en ubicaciones de Taco Bell en Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky, Ohio y West Virginia como fuente de brotes generalizados en esos estados. Michigan ha reportado 4,312 casos hasta el viernes, que son más que la cifra total nacional reportada por los CDC. Taylor Farms suministró lechuga a Taco Bell, informó The New York Times.</p><p>En un comunicado, Taco Bell anunció que retiraba de su cadena de suministro en todo el país la lechuga afectada y planeaba reemplazarla en ciertos estados.</p><p>Varios estados, incluyendo Illinois, han reportado casos no relacionados con ese grupo, dijo Biggerstaff, de los CDC. La agencia federal también está investigando otros brotes que podrían estar conectados entre sí.</p><p>Hasta el viernes, el Departamento de Salud Pública de Chicago no había identificado la fuente de los casos locales. Un individuo había comido en Taco Bell, pero también había viajado a uno de los estados que forman parte del brote mayor. El departamento está observando un aumento de casos entre latinos que no habían viajado recientemente al extranjero.</p><p>El número de casos, tanto a nivel local como en todo el país, podría ser mayor, dijo Landon. Eso se debe a que las pruebas para la ciclosporiasis son caras y algunos seguros pueden no cubrirlas. Pero a medida que los casos de ciclosporiasis están más en las noticias, es probable que los médicos comiencen a realizar más pruebas a los pacientes o a recetar antibióticos para tratarla si alguien presenta síntomas.</p><p>Si a una persona se le confirma que tiene ciclosporiasis, dijo Landon, es importante cooperar con el departamento de salud local para detallar todo lo que ha comido, para que las autoridades puedan identificar la fuente del brote.</p><h3>¿<b>Están los recortes federales afectando el brote? </b></h3><p>El verano pasado, el gobierno federal redujo un programa conocido como la Red de Vigilancia Activa de Enfermedades Transmitidas por Alimentos que monitoreaba enfermedades transmitidas por alimentos, <a class="Link" href="https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/cdc-quietly-scaled-back-surveillance-program-foodborne-illnesses-rcna227089?link_source=ta_bluesky_link&taid=68add0b9b2316600014ce6de&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_medium=social&utm_source=bluesky" target="_blank" >informó anteriormente NBC News</a>. Como parte de los cambios, el reporte de parásitos de ciclosporiasis pasó a ser opcional en 2025, según el sitio web del programa. El gobierno había recopilado esos datos desde 1997.</p><p>El programa federal reducido trabajó con la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos(FDA) para probar proactivamente ciertos alimentos y verificar si era necesaria su retirada, señaló Landon.</p><p>Es difícil evaluar hasta qué punto los cambios a nivel federal están influyendo en los brotes actuales, dijo Landon. Pero es algo que los funcionarios de salud en todo el país deberían considerar.</p><p>“Es una combinación de la índole de la enfermedad, del hecho de que ocurre en un momento en que hay otros casos esporádicos, y de la falta de infraestructura y recursos disponibles para realizar pruebas, lo cual sí importa”, destacó Landon, al resumir los factores que impulsan el brote.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" >La Voz Chicago</a></p>

entries.title: Chicago police officer among at least 2 shot during standoff at Albany Park home
entries.summary: <p>A Chicago police SWAT officer was among at least two people shot Monday morning when a suspect barricaded himself inside a home in the Albany Park neighborhood on the Northwest Side, according to a police alert.</p><p>Police responded around 11 a.m. to a home in the 4600 block of North Springfield Avenue, according to the internal alert. </p><p>The male suspect shot a female in the face and barricaded himself inside the home with a 13-year-old child, the police alert said. The SWAT officer was also shot, although the exact circumstances were unclear. </p><p>Both gunshot victims were taken to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center, according to the alert. Their conditions weren't immediately known.</p><p>By Monday afternoon, Ald. Rossana Rodriguez Sanchez (33rd) reported that a suspect had been taken into custody.</p><p>The wounded officer joined the police department in September 2005, according to the Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board. The Sun-Times isn't naming him because he's a crime victim. </p><p>Two other people were hurt and were taken to hospitals in unknown conditions, according to the Chicago Fire Department. They were not believed to be shot. </p><h3><b>‘We got a SWAT officer shot’</b></h3><p>Officers initially responded around 10:55 a.m. to a 911 call of a female shot in the face, according to police radio traffic. About 10 minutes later, a SWAT response was authorized to respond to a suspect barricaded inside the home.</p><p>During the standoff, a female called 911 from inside the home and could be heard pleading with the suspect.</p><p>“Please don’t shoot through the door,” the caller said.</p><p>“She is trying to convince him to put the gun down. Use caution, guys," a dispatcher told responding officers.</p><p>Around 11:45 a.m., an "officer in distress" call pierced through the airwaves.</p><p>“We got a SWAT officer shot guys, in the rear, we got a SWAT officer shot,” the dispatcher said.</p><h3><b>Neighbors feel unsafe</b></h3><p>Some neighbors drawn to the crime scene expressed concerns about crime in the Northwest Side neighborhood.</p><p>Alvin Woodley said he's lived in Albany Park for seven years and doesn’t always feel safe, especially at night. </p><p>Woodley, 56, recalled a boy being shot in the chest at a nearby park last year while children were playing basketball. He said neighbors may be hesitant to call police and report what they see.</p><p>"I think a lot of people just don't want to get involved," Woodley said. “The police station is right down the street, so there shouldn’t be that much crime.”</p><p>Another neighbor was more blunt: "I don't feel safe anywhere."</p><p>The 58-year-old man, who declined to give his name, said he has lived in the area for several years. He said he believes crime in the neighborhood has gotten worse, so he got a license to carry a gun in public.</p><p>"You have to take care of yourself," he said. "You can't depend on the police. It's not only here, it's everywhere."</p><p><i>This is a developing story, check back for details.</i> </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> entries.title: Connor Bedard 'very happy' with new contract, Blackhawks' summer additions
entries.summary: <p>On Monday, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks?_gl=1*1yf8vbg*_up*MQ..*_ga*NzQwODI1ODU1LjE3ODQ1NzIzOTA.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODQ1NzIzOTAkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODQ1NzIzOTAkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> star Connor Bedard had a $9.8 million signing bonus hitting his back account, an uncomfortable left shoulder dangling by his side and a sunny morning in Vancouver unfolding on the green trees behind him.</p><p>That's two reasons to be happy versus one reason to be unhappy. It added up to a lively first meeting with reporters since <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/19/connor-bedard-agent-explains-blackhawks-contract-shoulder-surgery-leo-carlsson?_gl=1*18567z*_up*MQ..*_ga*ODM4MzI1NTA0LjE3ODQ1NzE0NjQ.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODQ1NzE0NjMkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODQ1NzIzNTMkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >signing</a> his new five-year contract two days ago.</p><p>"I'm very happy with the amount of money I'm making. It's a lot," Bedard said, chuckling, before reiterating he didn't consider Ducks star Leo Carlsson's offer sheet comparable to his situation.</p><p>"Like I’ve said so much — and it's not anything fake — Chicago is really the only place I want to play. [That comes from] seeing the growth of our young guys and just how good of a group we are in the room, how tight it is, how much fun we have. I'm very happy to get this deal signed and just focus on the team."</p><p>Bedard described the negotiation process as not stressful, certainly less so than his decision to undergo surgery after his "frustrating" and fluky shoulder injury July 2.</p><p>"It’s a terrible part of the game," he said. "But for me, to have this next little bit and go through that adversity and try to get stronger mentally, that’s how I’m looking at it. And then [when I] come back ... [I'm] not going to be scared."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Connor Bedard, chuckling: "I'm very happy with the amount of money I'm making. It's a lot."<br><br>"Chicago is the only place I want to play... I'm very happy to get this deal signed and just focus on the team." <a href="https://t.co/334dqR6OZJ">pic.twitter.com/334dqR6OZJ</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2079251991016943751?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">July 20, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>He still plans to spend most of the rest of the offseason in Vancouver with his family and "a good team of people that the staff in Chicago feels comfortable with." Right now, his days are filled with physiotherapy sessions and workouts designed "to get this thing back to 100% as quick as possible."</p><p>Come training camp — which should start around Sept. 16 — he will join the Hawks in Chicago, and he thinks he could be cleared to skate individually by then.</p><p>"We want to take a big step this year," he said. "We want to be a playoff team, and that’s our only goal."</p><p>Bedard's belief in the Hawks' organizational direction is steadfast, as his agent Don Meehan <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/19/connor-bedard-agent-explains-blackhawks-contract-shoulder-surgery-leo-carlsson?_gl=1*14e9fr1*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTI1NzE2MDg4My4xNzg0NTcyOTk1*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODQ1NzI5OTUkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODQ1NzI5OTUkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >emphasized this weekend</a>, and Bedard repeatedly brought up Monday his excitement about the team's offseason additions.</p><p>"[Bowen Byram is] going to be one of the best 'D'-men in the league," Bedard said. "When you play behind Cale [Makar] and [Rasmus] Dahlin, it's not easy to take their spots. [It's big] for him to get that opportunity to be that No. 1 and prove himself in that way, and he's going to do it. He's one of the most skilled players in the league. His motivation to prove that is unbelievable."</p><p>Bedard also went out of his way to mention Jordan Greenway, Ian Cole and Cole Smith, the latter two having previously said Bedard reached out to them right after they signed.</p><p>"I think Ian Cole probably landed the most cross-checks on me out of anyone else in my life," Bedard said. "But now he's my teammate and we're both going to go to war for each other, which is the beautiful thing about hockey."</p><p>There's one more Hawks addition potentially coming: Patrick Kane, whom Chris Chelios has said is deciding between the Hawks and Sabres. And that idea made Bedard's eyes light up even more than they already were.</p><p>"I can't imagine [Kane's] first game back at the [United Center], the reaction he’d get and how much juice that would bring to not only our team but our fans, as well," Bedard said. "That would be incredible to play with him and learn from him.</p><p>"You [can] talk about the legacy aspect of it, but...he would make us a way better team. He's still an amazing player. I don’t know if this is the best pitch, but hopefully he comes back and we can play together."</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: SEC commissioner says league is seriously considering leaving NCAA
entries.summary: <p>TAMPA, Fla. — Southeastern Conference Commissioner Greg Sankey said Monday that leaders of the powerhouse league are having "real" conversations about breaking away from the rest of college sports, though that is not the preferred solution.</p><p>"They're real," Greg Sankey said Monday of talks with school presidents involving the SEC separating itself from the rest of the NCAA. "They've opined about the frustrations that bring them to the point of saying we should look at something significantly different."</p><p>Sankey's 45-minute meeting with reporters to kick off SEC football media days detailed the several issues that college sports is trying to find solutions for: Congressional legislation, litigation stemming from the new five-year eligibility rule, the future of the College Football Playoff and an overall lack of transparency regarding name, image and likeness payments to players.</p><p>Sankey acknowledged the conference's frustration with the handling of all those issues, but also touted the league's 13 national championships won last season across a variety of sports as a key reason it's in no rush to move away from the current framework.</p><p>"There is meaning and value and I do think a national expectation that we participate in a national organization," he said. "But that national organization must function in a healthy manner; otherwise, that simmering will continue".</p><p>The SEC has produced a 10-point paper about changes it would like to see to the Protect College Sports Act, a bipartisan piece of legislation in the Senate. The SEC and Big Ten are negotiating over with lawmakers over potential tweaks.</p><p>The SEC argues the bill does not go far enough in limiting the possibility of lawsuits against conferences and schools, and also needs better language to preempt state laws in favor of a national one regarding the tens of millions in NIL payments now so common at the top of college sports.</p><p>Sankey called the rollout of the recent NCAA rule that rewrote eligibility standards and has induced lawsuits — players mainly get five years to play five seasons — "magnifies frustration" among some in the SEC.</p><p>The SEC remains the Power Four's only holdout over expanding the 12-team playoff to 24. Sankey said more research is needed, especially regarding "media interest" — likely shorthand for media rights interest — in adding more games.</p><p>There is also the underlying issue of what an expanded playoff would do to conference title games. Symbolic of the wide range of opinions on that topic, Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said in his own media session that he favored conference play-in games to determine CFP spots and he doesn't think title games should be put on the chopping block.</p><p>"Throwing those away so you can get a bad matchup between 24 and 18 doesn't make sense to me," Drinkwitz said.</p><p>Sankey said he also wants more transparency about who pays players and for what. Among the SEC's proposed changes to the Senate bill would be clearer guidelines for paying players, including "NIL, pay-for-play (which is not allowed), revenue sharing and other forms of compensation."</p><p>The commissioner conceded that the SEC is not bent on getting its way regarding every issue that college sports is trying to solve. But as one of the biggest, richest and most influential leagues in a quickly changing business, it does want to lead the way.</p><p>"I think we do a better job now than has ever been done in college athletics," Sankey said. "But we haven't achieved that level of stability as we go through change that's needed at this point."<br></p>

entries.title: Tigers-Cubs game will be delayed because of weather in area
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs’</a> game Monday night against the Tigers at Wrigley Field will be delayed because of weather in the area. First pitch was scheduled for 7:05 p.m.</p><p>Jameson Taillon is set to make his first start since June 7, when he left after one inning because of a strained left hamstring. He'll face the Tigers' Jack Flaherty. </p><p>Both teams are coming off series in which they took two of three games. The Cubs won the last two against the Twins at home, while the Tigers won the first two against the Angels in Anaheim.</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module entries.title: Colson Montgomery’s All-Star snub firing him up for White Sox' second-half surge
entries.summary: <p>ARLINGTON, Texas — Colson Montgomery didn’t need another chip on his shoulder, but he’ll take it.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a>’ lanky shortstop has heard his whole career that he’s too big to stick at his position, that his hefty strikeout rate would keep him from being a viable big-leaguer and, entering this season, that his team wasn’t going anywhere.</p><p>Most recently, despite leading MLB shortstops in home runs, Montgomery has been told he’s not an All-Star, giving the 24-year-old one more thing to prove people wrong about.</p><p>After launching out of the break in Toronto with a loaded-bases-clearing double and a timely home run — No. 24 of his sophomore campaign — Montgomery said his All-Star snub is motivating him in the second half “as it should.”</p><p>“As a competitor, you should see yourself as the best, because if you don't, you're just selling yourself short,” Montgomery said before the Sox returned stateside for a three-game set with the Rangers. “You're not really giving yourself the inner confidence that you need to play this game, especially with how much it can just beat you down.”</p><p>That’s coming from somebody who knows it. The Sox’ 2021 first-round draft pick took a beating at the plate at the beginning of last season, when his dismal start at Triple-A Charlotte prompted Sox brass <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/03/28/colson-montgomery-white-sox-year-2" target="_blank" ><u>to pull him from game action altogether</u></a> to regroup at their Arizona training complex.</p><p>Since then, Montgomery has established himself one of baseball’s most productive shortstops at the plate while flashing more leather than the Sox could’ve expected.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colson Montgomery goes deep! <a href="https://t.co/rEuUrBtC7V">pic.twitter.com/rEuUrBtC7V</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://x.com/whitesox/status/2078896606393295089?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">July 19, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>His two-run bomb at the Rogers Centre on Sunday was the 45th of his career, coming just a few days shy of a year since slugging <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2025/07/22/colson-montgomery-first-homer-white-sox-streak" target="_blank" ><u>his first career MLB home run</u></a> on July 22, 2025, at Tampa. Only Kyle Schwarber (57) and Junior Caminero (49) logged more dingers over that time, according to MLB statistician Sarah Langs.</p><p>Montgomery’s work before the break still wasn’t enough to get him an All-Star nod <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/14/white-sox-all-stars-munetaka-murakami-miguel-vargas-tristan-peters-mlb-philadelphia-citizens-bank-park" target="_blank" ><u>alongside teammates</u></a> Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami and Tristan Peters. Adding salt to the wound were the pair of division rival shortstops who got in ahead of Montgomery: Royals superstar Bobby Witt Jr. (.280/.350/.451 with 13 homers entering play Monday) and Tigers rookie Kevin McGonigle (.282/.390/.425, nine homers).</p><p>Aside from his position-leading homer total, Montgomery arrived in Texas with the third-most RBI (57) and fourth-highest slugging percentage (.477) among shortstops.</p><p>“Of course I thought I should have been, but obviously it didn't work out, and all I can do now is just respond,” Montgomery said. “I take that as like a little chip on my shoulder, I guess.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-1b0000" himself, “but if that's something out there that can give him an extra boost and put that chip on his shoulder, that's great.”</p><p>“There are still lots of awesome awards you can go out and win by having a really good second half here,” Venable said. “He's already done so much for us this year.”</p><p>Not helping Montgomery’s All-Star case were his 121 punchouts before the break, second-most among shortstops and in the top six overall, symptomatic of his streaky nature at the plate.</p><p>“I've come to realize that I'm not sure how to characterize where Colson's at,” Venable said. “There are some at-bats where he looks maybe out of sync, and then in the same game, he's hitting the game-winning homer. … He's doing what he's doing, which is getting big hits for us and driving in runs.”</p><p>Montgomery acknowledged a few days off provided “a very good refresher mentally,” not just for him, but for a clubhouse shouldering plenty of chips while stunning a baseball world that had them inked for another season of cellar-dwelling back in March.</p><p>“It just goes back to everyone [outside] still doubting a little,” Montgomery said. “We're a good team, we've had success and we're very confident in ourselves. And I think that's what's most dangerous about a team, especially a young team. … I think we all have a chip on our shoulder just because we want to keep proving everyone wrong, and prove ourselves right from spring training. entries.title: Six heat-related deaths in Cook County mark July as the deadliest month in more than a decade
entries.summary: <p>Six people in Cook County have died from heat-related causes in July so far, marking the deadliest stretch of extreme hot-weather deaths since at least 2015.</p><p>Victor Ferguson is the latest person identified who died amid the scorching heat wave earlier this month. Ferguson died July 2 from a heat stroke with ethanol intoxication as a secondary cause, according to new records from the Cook County medical examiner’s office. He was 48.</p><p>Four of the six people who died were younger than 60 . In all six July deaths logged in Cook County so far, the high temperature ranged from 88 to 95 degrees on the day they either died or were hospitalized, according to an analysis of National Weather Service data by WBEZ and the Chicago Sun-Times. During that first week of July, heading into the July 4 weekend, Cook County was under an extreme heat warning.</p><p>Besides Ferguson, the others whose deaths have been attributed to the heat are Stephanie Rodriguez, 45; David Gonzalez, 44; Barbara Whigham, 71; Mike Rodriguez, 57; and Daniel Machnikowski, 69, according to the medical examiner's office.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-3a0000" name="html-embed-module-3a0000"></a><div class="flourish-embed flourish-chart" data-src="visualisation/29744387"><script src="https://public.flourish.studio/resources/embed.js"></script><noscript><img src="https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/29744387/thumbnail" width="100%" alt="chart visualization" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><p>Since Chicago’s 1995 heat wave that killed more than 700 people, the city has suffered through at least two other major deadly heat waves: <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/8/30/18354264/a-look-back-at-chicago-s-deadly-1995-heat-wave" target="_blank" ><u>in 1999, when 10 people died, and in 2012, when 22 died.</u></a></p><p>Marc Raifman, who works with the Extreme Weather Planners Coalition, said city officials should work with community members to examine the circumstances that led to the deaths earlier this month.</p><p>“Why aren’t we looking at these cases, figuring out in some level of detail the same way they do in the medical field, what went wrong that led someone to experience a heat or cold injury that in some awful cases took their life,” Raifman said. “And what can we do to prevent that next time and save the next person?”</p><p>Ferguson lived in the East Garfield Park neighborhood on the West Side. His family could not be immediately reached. </p><p>Neighbors recalled Ferguson living with his family in a limestone two-flat home. Air conditioning units could be seen on the first and second floors. </p><p>Neighbors said Ferguson often was seen walking his two dogs.</p><p>Neighbors of Rodriguez said he shared a home with several relatives. Rodriguez, they added, lived in the attic, which didn't have great air circulation. An air conditioning unit could be seen mounted in an attic window Monday morning.</p><p>Relatives and friends for the others who died either declined to comment or couldn’t be reached, including a relative of Rodriguez who lived in the same home and declined to comment Monday.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a A window air conditioner can be seen in the front window of the attic, where neighbors said Mike Rodriguez lived.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>One death happened in Evanston and the other five people who died were residents of Chicago’s South and West sides. Communities in Chicago’s South and West sides are most vulnerable to extreme heat, said Daniel Horton, an associate professor at Northwestern University who helped develop a heat vulnerability index for the city.</p><p>Some of that vulnerability is tied to socioeconomic factors, like not being able to afford an elevated electricity bill to cool a home or not having an adequate air conditioning unit, Horton said. Neighborhoods with fewer trees also provide less shade during extreme heat, which is one reason community groups advocate for more shading near bus stops.</p><p>But a bigger issue to tackle is social isolation, Horton said, referencing one of the larger issues that came out of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2015/7/11/18609460/chicago-1995-heat-wave-anniversary" target="_blank" ><u>devastating 1995 heat wave</u></a>. People were more likely to have died if they weren’t connected to neighbors who could check on them or give them a fan or other materials to help them stay cool.</p><p>“That social infrastructure piece of it is also really key to increasing a community’s resilience,” Horton said.</p><p>Community groups have also pushed not only for a 24-hour cooling center but also for one that stays open during weekends or holidays, Raifman said. The city has standards for activating an emergency response due to weather but those standards can feel unattainable, he said.</p><p>The city sometimes extends closing hours to 8 p.m. for its community service center at 10 S. Kedzie Ave., according to the mayor’s office.</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson’s office also said officials were closely monitoring high temperatures, adding that they consider police districts, libraries, community colleges and park district facilities to be part of citywide cooling efforts. In a statement, the mayor’s office said it was “deeply saddened by any weather-related loss of life in our city,” and offered condolences.</p><p>“There are leaders and individuals at the city who are certainly working hard, in the moment, to address these things,” Raifman said. “But I think what they lack and what we lack is any kind of advance planning and understanding of what gets deployed where.”</p><p><i>Contributing: Cam Rodriguez, Mohammad Samra, Alden Loury</i></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/07/10/fifth-heat-related-death-recorded-in-chicago-area" >Fifth heat-related death recorded in Chicago area</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2025/07/11/chicago-heat-wave-1995-deaths-brandon-johnson-northwestern-university-climate-change" >30 years after historic heat wave, Chicagoans are still at risk</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
